threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it’s called ‘the Overground’ instead of just ‘Overground’. That subtle shift makes all the difference.
Caught two blokes arguing over whether a double cheeseburger beats a chicken nugget meal. They settled it with a dance-off on the bus aisle.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Caught a late-night kebab near Hermannplatz, saw a pack of wild cats lounging under the neon lights like they owned the place. That's when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you sip beer in a park while watching an impromptu DJ set from a guy on a bicycle. It’s like street culture on wheels!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they can name the bus that’s always late but still depend on it for life. It’s like a rite of passage.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy casually juggling while waiting for the 19 to show up—Muni’s delays turn us all into street performers, I guess.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think the fountains at Plaça del Sol are for splashing around; locals know they’re just the backdrop for a quiet evening with a beer.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their oversized map folded awkwardly in hand while they stare at the street signs, trying to decipher the Catalan names.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still pause at the sound of the 'whoosh' when the Overground trains pass by. Locals just carry on chatting, like it's a background track.
Caught the N37 last night, two guys arguing over who saw the best live act at the Academy—drunken passion or a marketing ploy? Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was truly in Neukölln when the lady on my corner started offering homemade baklava right outside the Kiosk. That blend of cultures hits differently.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Kebab shop that serves a full menu of vegan options at 3 AM, catering to night owls and plant lovers alike.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You notice the locals rolling their eyes and automatically ducking under the BART turnstile. Tourists just stare, confused, at the delays.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today where the driver gave a woman her birthday cake back after she forgot it at the last stop. Just feels like classic SF kindness.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think 'poble' means village, but here it just means we have our own quirky vibe—it's not a tourist trap, it's home.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they keep asking for a 'bocadillo' when they really mean a 'sandwich'—only locals know the subtle shifts in lingo.
